name: ImpulseMoveOutOfEquilibrium
quote: Eventually, there is a failure of liquidity on one side, and the market makes a sudden, large movement in one direction... this type of sharp movement is called an impulse move or a momentum move.
description: A sharp, large-range directional move that breaks a market out of a quiet, range-bound (equilibrium) state -- the trigger event the book treats as the start of a possible trend. No numeric threshold is given in this chapter for 'sudden' or 'large'; a natural proxy is a bar (or short run of bars) whose range or net move exceeds a multiple of recent average range/ATR after a period of contraction.
pseudocode: priorRangeContracted(...)  AND (high[0]-low[0]) > impulseAtrMultiple * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: the concept is real and named ('impulse move') but Grimes gives no numeric threshold in this chapter; both the contraction test and the impulse-size test need a design decision before this is codeable

notes: This is the qualitative seed of the whole book's trend-structure chapters (3, 5); kept research-grade rather than rejected because Grimes treats it as the mechanical trigger of the whole market cycle.

name: HighAndTightFlagPullback
quote: one or two small bars that hold near the extreme of a trend leg (near the lows in a downtrend or the highs in an uptrend) are often a complete lower time frame pullback. As such, these simple one- or two-bar pullbacks (high and tight flags) are tradable structures in very strong trends.
description: In a strong uptrend, one or two consecutive small-range bars that hold near the most recent swing high (rather than making a deep retracement) constitute a complete, tradable pullback; mirrored near swing lows in a downtrend.
pseudocode: isUptrend(...) AND count(isSmallBarNearRecentHigh, lag=0..(pullbackBars-1)) == pullbackBars  where isSmallBarNearRecentHigh := (high[lag]-low[lag]) < smallBarAtrFraction*atr(atrLookback) AND (highest(high[1],swingLookback) - low[lag]) < nearAtrFraction*atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: needs an uptrend test, pivot/swing-high detection, and a multi-bar small-range-near-extreme window test

notes: Chapter 3 (mined separately) is expected to give the precise, general pullback taxonomy; this is Chapter 1's specific example of the shallowest form.

name: ComplexPullbackThreeLegStructure
quote: Another important pullback pattern in an uptrend has several bars with downward closes separated by a single bar with an upward close... From that second leg, the market turns down again to make another countertrend leg that is usually approximately as long as the first one.
description: A complex, two-legged countertrend pullback in an uptrend: a run of down-closing bars, then one bar closing up (a small failed resumption attempt), then a second down-closing leg of roughly the same length/depth as the first. Mirrored for a downtrend.
pseudocode: downLegLength(leg1) > 0 AND upBarsBetween == 1 AND downLegLength(leg2) approximately equals downLegLength(leg1)  // 'approximately equals' left as a tolerance parameter

complexity.reason: needs run-length counting for two legs plus a tolerance comparison between their lengths, and 'approximately as long' is not numerically specified

notes: Chapter 3 (mined separately, 'Trading Complex Pullbacks' is actually Chapter 6) is expected to define this precisely; this is Chapter 1's informal preview, kept per the high-recall instruction.

name: TrendContinuationPullbackContext
quote: Perhaps the most common trend continuation play is to use the pullbacks in a trend to position for further trend legs.
description: The trend-continuation trade category's framework-level definition: an entry with the trend (G02-02) taken on a pullback. The precise pullback structure (simple vs. complex, depth as a fraction of the prior swing, first pullback after a breakout) is left to Chapter 3 (mined separately); this candidate records only the cycle-level statement that ties the trade category to the phase.
pseudocode: MarkupMarkdownTrendPhase(...) AND isPullback(...)  // isPullback left abstract, defined precisely in Chapter 3

complexity.reason: depends on both a trend definition and a pullback definition, neither given a precise numeric form in this chapter

notes: Kept for completeness per the mining brief's instruction to define each of the four trades precisely; the actual pullback mechanics are expected from Chapter 3's mining pass, and the dedup pass should treat this as a coarse duplicate of whatever specific pullback-entry rules that chapter produces.
chapter_title: The Market Cycle and the Four Trades

name: TrendContinuationRiskAtSwingInvalidation
quote: The key to defining risk is to define the points at which the trend trade is conclusively wrong, at which the trend is violated.
description: The stop for a trend-continuation trade sits beyond the swing point (the pullback low in an uptrend / pullback high in a downtrend) that defined the entry -- the point at which the trend thesis is falsified.
pseudocode: close[0] <= swingLowSinceEntry - stopBuffer
book_order_type: stop beyond the invalidating swing point, mechanized as close-then-next-open

complexity.reason: reads a swing/pivot level established at or before entry and tracked across the position's life

chapter_title: The Market Cycle and the Four Trades

name: ClimaxAfterMultipleTrendLegsComposite
quote: Usually come after two or more trend legs in the same direction. Show an acceleration in the direction of the previous trend.
description: Composite climax condition: two or more prior trend legs in the same direction (needs leg/pivot counting, a design decision), plus acceleration, large range bars, free bars, and closes bunched at the bar extreme. Grimes's summary checklist for identifying a climax/exhaustion top or bottom.
pseudocode: priorTrendLegCount >= 2 AND (G03-05 OR G03-04) AND (G03-02 OR G03-06)

complexity.reason: leg counting needs a swing/pivot detector and a design decision for what counts as a 'trend leg'; the component tests are otherwise mechanical

notes: Grimes also notes climaxes 'vary in significance' and are rare mid-range (usually at a significant new high/low) -- both are further design decisions left for authoring.

name: AvoidPullbackAfterClimax
quote: Do not enter pullbacks following potential climaxes.
description: Block with-trend pullback entries for N bars after a climax condition (G03-08) fires.
pseudocode: barsSince(lastClimaxFired) >= coolOffBars

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-08

name: AvoidPullbackAfterDivergence
quote: suggests that long trades should not be entered on the next pullback
description: Block with-trend pullback entries when the most recent new price extreme was accompanied by a momentum divergence (G03-13).
pseudocode: barsSince(lastDivergenceFired) <= sinceDivergenceBars ? false : true

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-13

name: PullbackFollowsStrongImpulseFilter
quote: trade only pullbacks that are preceded by significant momentum in the direction of the trend
description: Only take with-trend pullback entries when the impulse leg preceding the pullback was accompanied by G03-12 (momentum indicator registering a new extreme) within a recent lookback.
pseudocode: barsSince(lastMomentumExtreme) <= momPrecedeBars

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-12

name: SimplePullbackPrimitive
quote: A pullback is a countertrend movement ... in a trend that usually leads to another price movement in the direction of the original trend
description: Primitive: a pullback is a run of bars moving against the established trend direction following an impulse leg. Approximated here as consecutive lower closes with no new trend-direction extreme; downstream candidates refer to this by id rather than redefining it.
pseudocode: close[0] < close[1] AND close[0] < highest(close, pullbackBars)[1]

complexity.reason: true pullback identification needs swing-pivot detection to mark the start and end of the countertrend leg; this is a consecutive-bar/no-new-extreme proxy

name: ComplexPullbackTwoLegged
quote: the complex pullback, which is a standard pullback followed by a failed attempt to resume the original trend. When this attempt fails and rolls over, the pullback puts in a second leg against the larger trend
description: After a pullback (G03-16) and a failed resumption attempt (price tries but fails to make a new trend-direction extreme), the market makes a second countertrend leg beyond the first pullback's extreme -- a complex ('two-legged') pullback.
pseudocode: pivotLow2 < pivotLow1 AND priceAttemptedNewHighBetween(pivot1, pivot2) AND thatAttemptFailed

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection over a variable-length window plus a fail/resume state machine

notes: Also called a 'two-legged pullback'; Elliott's alternation rule (simple/complex pullbacks alternate through an extended trend) is noted by Grimes but is not itself a bar-level test -- left as a note for the authoring pass, not a separate candidate.

name: PullbackLowerActivityFilter
quote: they are generally periods of lower activity compared to trend legs
description: Valid pullback bars should show a smaller average range than the average range of the preceding impulse leg's bars.
pseudocode: average(high-low, pullbackBars) < contractionFraction * average(high-low, impulseLegBars)

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection to separately identify pullback-leg bars vs. the preceding impulse-leg bars

name: FlatPullbackStallsIntoRange
quote: the market begins what looks like a good pullback but then there is simply no move out of that pullback. Instead, the market goes into a flat range
description: After a pullback of N bars, price has failed to make a new trend-direction extreme and recent bar ranges have contracted to a narrow band -- the pullback has stalled into a range; exit or avoid new with-trend entries.
pseudocode: barsSince(pullbackStart) > stallBars AND NOT newExtremeSince(pullbackStart) AND average(high-low, recentBars) < tightMultiple*average(high-low, priorBars)
book_order_type: market at next open once flagged, per convention

complexity.reason: needs a pullback-start pivot plus a persistent no-new-extreme flag

name: GapDoesNotFillContinuationSignal
quote: Are there gaps up that do not fill on a daily chart?
description: An opening gap in the trend direction that is not filled (price never trades back through the pre-gap close) within N bars -- a sign of strong conviction/continuation.
pseudocode: open[0] > close[1] AND lowest(low, fillLookback) > close[1]

complexity.reason: a rolling lowest/highest window since the gap

name: DiagonalSlopingRangeComplexPullback
quote: the diagonal range sloping against the higher time frame trend ... could be considered the most common pullback pattern
description: A parallel trading range whose slope runs counter to the higher-timeframe trend is, functionally, a complex pullback (G03-17) playing out on the trading timeframe. Springs near support (or upthrusts near resistance) within it are especially strong with-trend entries (see G04-21).
pseudocode: G04-10 (bounded range) AND rangeSlope opposes htfTrendDirection

complexity.reason: combines range detection with a slope-of-range measure and a higher-timeframe direction read

notes: Cross-chapter composite: reuses Chapter 3's complex-pullback definition (G03-17) rather than redefining it.

name: ContinuationRangeHigherTimeframeCheck
quote: the higher time frame will often tell a simple story: the trading time frame trend may have pushed the higher time frame into an overbought or overextended condition, and the unreadable range on the trading time frame is actually just a simple pullback on the higher time frame
description: An otherwise-unreadable trading-timeframe range is treated as a continuation (pullback) pattern when the higher-timeframe proxy (G03-35, a much longer moving-average slope) still agrees with the prior trend direction.
pseudocode: G04-10 (bounded range) AND htfTrendDirection (G03-35 test) == priorTrendDirection

complexity.reason: inherits G03-35's higher-timeframe design decision

name: ShrinkingPullbacksIntoResistance
quote: prices holding higher lows into a more or less clearly defined resistance level... the declines will become shallower simply because more people are buying them.
description: Each successive pullback low within a trading range is higher than the prior pullback low while the range high stays roughly flat -- an ascending-triangle accumulation pattern preceding a good breakout.
pseudocode: swingLow[0] > swingLow[1] > swingLow[2] AND abs(swingHigh[0] - swingHigh[1]) < flatTolerance * avgRange AND abs(swingHigh[1] - swingHigh[2]) < flatTolerance * avgRange

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and multi-leg comparison

notes: Grimes gives no exact swing count for the 'ascending triangle' quality; 3 is a reasonable default.

name: PullbackHoldsOutsideBreakoutLevel
quote: The market breaks through the level, trades sharply beyond the level, and then makes a clean pullback that holds outside the breakout level.
description: Since the breakout entry, every bar's low (long) / high (short) has stayed beyond the breakout level, never trading back across it -- the cleanest, easiest-to-manage first pullback.
pseudocode: lowest(low, ctx.BarsSinceEntry()) > breakoutLevel

complexity.reason: needs the breakout level carried as position state and a since-entry window

name: StrongMomentumConfirmsBreakoutPullbackContinuation
quote: It is far more common to see these pullbacks fail with very strong momentum out of the pattern or fail on a second test of the extreme reached after the pullback.
description: The pullback following a breakout resolves with a strong-momentum bar in the breakout direction (large body relative to recent average range) -- confirms trend continuation and re-entry.
pseudocode: close[0] > close[1] AND (close[0] - open[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback])
book_order_type: n/a (context test) or entry on the close of this bar -> close-and-next-open

complexity.reason: single-bar body vs. window-average range

name: SharpCountertrendBreaksBreakoutPullback
quote: C marks a classic breakout pullback failure, as sharp downside momentum breaks out of the bottom of the pullback.
description: Point C: within the post-breakout pullback, a bar breaks below the pullback's own low so far with strong momentum against the breakout direction -- an early warning that the breakout is failing.
pseudocode: low[0] < lowest(low[1], barsSincePullbackStart) AND (open[0] - close[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback])

complexity.reason: needs the pullback's own start tracked since the breakout

name: FailurePullbackCountertrendEntry
quote: Shorting into the pullback at D is a good trade based just on that criterion, but, in this case, it is further motivated by the failure of the breakout level at A.
description: Point D: after G05-15 fires, the first small pullback in the new (countertrend-to-the-original-breakout) direction is a tradable entry against the failed breakout.
pseudocode: G05-15[n] fired AND this is the first pullback since bar n against the new (post-failure) direction
book_order_type: n/a (composite context; actual trigger inherits pullback-entry conventions)

complexity.reason: requires tracking a short-term trend change and detecting its first pullback

notes: This is the same pattern Chapter 6 names the 'Failure Pullback' inside the Failed Breakouts template; recorded independently here per the mining brief.

name: TrendLegCountCaution
quote: After many directional pushes (more than three), it is likely that the market needs further consolidation before continuing the trend; the probability of pullback failure becomes higher with each subsequent trend leg.
description: The count of same-direction trend legs since the last opposite-direction leg exceeds a threshold -- raises the odds the next pullback fails; a caution filter reducing confidence in fresh with-trend pullback entries.
pseudocode: sameDirectionLegCount > maxLegs

complexity.reason: needs swing-leg counting

name: PullbackStallsIntoRange
quote: There is simply no move out of the pullback as prices stabilize around a price level in the pullback itself.
description: After a trend, the pullback's own range fails to expand for N bars -- its high-low envelope stops making new extremes in either direction -- the pullback is transitioning directly into a trading range rather than resuming the trend.
pseudocode: highest(high, stallBars) - lowest(low, stallBars) < stallFraction * trendLegRange

complexity.reason: 'trading range' is a design-level concept; this is a range-contraction proxy

name: HighVolatilityBeforePullbackWarnsFailure
quote: Other common conditions preceding failed pullbacks are extremely high volatility, indicating possible climax or exhaustion.
description: ATR is elevated well above its own average immediately before a pullback begins -- a climax/exhaustion warning that raises the odds the pullback fails.
pseudocode: atr(atrLookback) > atrMultiple * average(atr(atrLookback), avgLookback)

complexity.reason: ATR of an ATR average

name: AcceleratingTrendLegSteepness
quote: they last a long time and they accelerate into a steeper trend before the actual expansion. This acceleration can either be a series of ever-steeping trend legs.
description: Each successive with-trend leg's slope (price change divided by bar count) is steeper than the previous leg's -- a warning sign the market may be primed for a parabolic blow-off.
pseudocode: legSlope[0] > legSlope[1] > legSlope[2], where legSlope = (legEndPrice - legStartPrice) / legBarCount

complexity.reason: needs swing-leg detection plus a slope comparison across an unspecified number of legs

notes: Related to the existing TrendLineSlopeFlattening rule but in the opposite sense (steepening, not flattening).

name: TriangleConsolidationAfterOppositeImpulses
quote: If a market makes a sharp move, followed by an almost equally sharp move in the opposite direction, there is a very high probability of an extended consolidation.
description: Two consecutive impulse legs of similar magnitude in opposite directions (a sharp move immediately reversed by an almost-equally sharp move) -- blocks new entries, since an extended, low-edge consolidation is likely to follow. Most common after parabolic climaxes.
pseudocode: abs(leg1Length - leg2Length) < similarityFraction * max(leg1Length, leg2Length) AND sign(leg1) != sign(leg2) AND leg2BarCount <= maxLegBars

complexity.reason: needs swing-leg detection and magnitude comparison

notes: Related to but distinct from ExpandingTrianglePattern -- this is a two-leg contraction test, not an expanding pattern.

name: SetupLegAtLeastAsStrongAsPriorLegs
quote: if the market is in an established trend, the preceding setup leg should be at least as strong as previous trend legs in the same direction. In other words, it should not break the pattern of the trend and should not show momentum divergence.
description: Pullback setup: the trend leg immediately preceding the pullback is at least as large (price extent) as the average of the preceding same-direction legs.
pseudocode: setupLegLength >= average(priorSameDirectionLegLengths, numPriorLegs)

complexity.reason: needs swing-leg detection and length comparison across several legs

name: PullbackReducedRangeActivity
quote: Good pullbacks almost always show reduced activity (smaller ranges for individual bars) and the absence of strong countertrend momentum.
description: The average bar range during the pullback is smaller than the average bar range of the preceding setup leg.
pseudocode: average(high[0..pullbackBars-1] - low[0..pullbackBars-1]) < reducedFraction * average(high[pullbackBars..pullbackBars+legBars-1] - low[pullbackBars..pullbackBars+legBars-1])

complexity.reason: two window range averages

name: AvoidThreeOrMoreSupportTestsInPullback
quote: One pattern to avoid is buying against multiple (three or more) tests of support in a pullback, as this pattern is often more indicative of an impending failure. The operative concept here is usually lower highs into support.
description: Do not take the pullback support-bounce trigger (G06-04) if the pullback has already tested its own support/resistance level maxTests or more times, with each bounce's high (low) lower (higher) than the previous.
pseudocode: testCount(low[i] near pullbackSupport, i = 0..pullbackBars) >= maxTests AND bounceHigh[0] < bounceHigh[1]

complexity.reason: needs a touch counter plus lower-highs (higher-lows) comparison across bounces

name: PullbackTemplate
quote: Pullbacks are probably the most important structural feature of trends... using the countertrend pullback to position in the larger trend at an advantageous price.
description: The book's named Pullback (Buying Support or Shorting Resistance) template in full: setup (strong setup leg G06-14, reduced pullback activity G06-15, avoid 3+ support tests G06-16) + trigger (trend-line failure reversal G06-03 OR support bounce G06-04) + stop (G06-17) + targets (conservative prior swing G06-18, risk-multiple G06-19, MMO G06-02) + management (scratch on integrity loss G06-20).
book_order_type: mixed: G06-03 is stop/market on the close-back bar, G06-04 is a limit entry

complexity.reason: aggregates hard leg-comparison setup conditions with the trend-line-proxy trigger

notes: Trade type: trend continuation. Encompasses flags, pennants, wedges, and continuation triangles per the book -- Grimes treats them as functionally identical, so no separate candidates were made for each named shape.

name: EqualHighsBreakoutWithinPullback
quote: if a series of two to three bars all have the same high, paying a breakout through those highs is often a good entry.
description: Two to three consecutive bars within the pullback share (approximately) the same high; enter on a breakout above that shared high.
pseudocode: abs(high[1] - high[2]) < tickTolerance * ctx.MinMove() AND close[0] > highest(high[1], equalBarsCount)
book_order_type: stop entry on the breakout of the equal highs -> close-and-next-open

complexity.reason: small-window equality test plus a breakout comparison

name: WiderStopTrueToPatternGeometry
quote: My preference is to use a larger stop that is true to the geometry of the trading time frame pattern.
description: Grimes's preferred stop for the lower-time-frame breakout entry: the standard pullback stop (G06-17), sized to the trading-time-frame pattern rather than the tight lower-time-frame trigger bar.
pseudocode: same as G06-17: stopPrice = lowest(low, pullbackLookback) - bufferAtrMultiple * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: same as G06-17

name: PullbackLtfBreakoutTemplate
quote: This trade setup addresses the key issue of precisely timing the entry into the pullback pattern.
description: The book's named Pullback, Entering Lower Time Frame Breakout template: same pullback setup as G06-21 (G06-14, G06-15) + trigger on a lower-time-frame breakout (G06-22 OR the equal-highs variant G06-23) + stop (tight G06-24 OR the preferred wider G06-25) + standard pullback targets (G06-18, G06-19, G06-02).
pseudocode: G06-14 AND G06-15 AND (G06-22 OR G06-23), managed by G06-25 (preferred) or G06-24, with G06-18/G06-19/G06-02 as targets
book_order_type: stop entry on the lower-time-frame breakout -> close-and-next-open

complexity.reason: inherits the hard pullback setup plus the LTF-approximation trigger

notes: Trade type: trend continuation and breakout blend. Better momentum confirmation, worse trade location and larger stops than the plain Pullback template.

name: ComplexPullbackAbcdTwoLegs
quote: A complex pullback is a complete ABCD trend structure itself: the first countertrend leg is a lower time frame trend... followed by a retracement... which is then followed by another countertrend leg.
description: The pullback contains two distinct countertrend legs separated by a with-trend retracement (an ABCD structure) rather than one simple leg.
pseudocode: swingLow[0] (D) exists after a with-trend retracement swingHigh[1] (C) that followed an earlier countertrend swingLow[2] (B) off swingHigh[3] (A), all within the pullback window

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and leg sequencing

name: HiddenComplexPullbackCandleColorCue
quote: This second complex pullback pattern is one or two with-trend candles in the middle of what otherwise looks like a simple pullback.
description: One or two bars with a body colored in the trend direction (close beyond open in the trend's direction) appear in the middle of an otherwise simple, against-trend-colored pullback -- a cue that the pullback is complex even though it looks simple on the trading time frame.
pseudocode: count(i = midStart..midEnd, sign(close[i] - open[i]) == trendDirection) between 1 and 2, while the bars flanking that window are colored against the trend

complexity.reason: a bar-body-direction sequence test over a small fixed window

name: AvoidSimplePullbackAfterClimax
quote: It is usually a good idea to avoid pullbacks after conditions that could indicate a buying or selling climax.
description: Block the simple Pullback template (G06-21) if a climax bar (G06-06) occurred within the recent lookback; a with-trend trade is still possible, but only via the complex-pullback template (G06-32), not the simple one.
pseudocode: NOT (any of the last climaxLookback bars satisfies ClimaxBarCondition)

complexity.reason: a short OR-window over the climax primitive

name: ComplexPullbackTemplate
quote: Complex pullbacks, which are pullbacks composed of two distinct countertrend legs, are very common, especially in mature trends.
description: The book's named Trading Complex Pullbacks template: setup (two-leg ABCD structure G06-27, or the hidden candle-color cue G06-28; may follow a climax where the simple template G06-21 is blocked by G06-29) + trigger (support bounce G06-04 or trend-line failure reversal G06-03, same as the simple pullback) + stop (G06-31, clearer than the simple pullback's) + target (leg-equality MMO, G06-30).
book_order_type: mixed: G06-03 is stop/market on the close-back bar, G06-04 is a limit entry

complexity.reason: requires swing-pivot detection for the ABCD structure

notes: Trade type: trend continuation. The book flags a real risk-management question -- taking this trade shortly after a loss on the simple pullback that preceded it -- but that reduces to position sizing and is not mechanized (see rejected).

name: AntiFirstPullbackTrigger
quote: The actual entry for this trade is in the first pullback following the strong countertrend price movement.
description: After G06-33 and G06-34 both fire, enter on the first pullback following the countertrend spike, using either standard pullback trigger (trend-line failure reversal G06-03, or support/resistance bounce G06-04).
pseudocode: G06-33 AND G06-34 fired recently AND (G06-03 OR G06-04) on the first pullback since the spike
book_order_type: mixed: G06-03 is stop/market on the close-back bar, G06-04 is a limit entry

complexity.reason: combines two hard setup conditions with a pullback trigger

name: AntiLooseEntryAnywhereInPullback
quote: Because this is a countertrend trade, your risk point is clearly defined so you can simply enter anywhere into that first pullback with a stop outside the existing trend extreme.
description: The Anti's third, loosest trigger: once the setup (G06-33, G06-34) has fired, enter at the next bar's open during the first pullback, without waiting for a specific trigger bar, using a stop beyond the trend extreme.
pseudocode: G06-33 AND G06-34 fired recently AND ctx.MarketPosition() == 0 -> enter at next open
book_order_type: market entry at the next bar's open

complexity.reason: a direct entry once the setup condition is true, no additional trigger bar test

notes: The book calls this 'not ideal in most cases.'

name: AntiProtectProfitsIfMmoHolds
quote: If, however, it holds and there is no continued countertrend momentum (and the pattern suggests a complex consolidation), be very protective of any remaining profits in the position.
description: If price reaches the MMO zone (G06-38) but fails to break through it (no new countertrend extreme within a few bars), tighten the stop to breakeven or better on the remaining position.
pseudocode: priceReachedMmoZone == true AND ctx.BarsSinceEntry() - mmoReachedBar > confirmBars AND close[0] has not exceeded the MMO zone -> tighten stop to ctx.EntryPrice()

complexity.reason: cross-bar state tracking whether the MMO zone was reached and then held

name: AntiTemplate
quote: This trade is a very specific pullback variation that attempts to enter the first pullback after a potential trend change.
description: The book's named Anti template in full: setup (trend-termination precondition G06-33, then a stronger-than-usual countertrend spike G06-34) + trigger (standard pullback trigger G06-35, or the loose anywhere-in-pullback entry G06-36) + stop (beyond the trend extreme, G06-37) + targets (MMO of the first thrust G06-38, with profit protection if it holds, G06-39).

complexity.reason: aggregates several hard swing-based setup conditions

notes: Trade type: trend termination. Named for Linda Raschke's 'Anti' (Street Smarts, 1996); see G06-62 for her original stochastic-divergence definition, recorded separately since Grimes himself prefers the pure price-structure form given here.

name: FirstPullbackAfterBreakoutTrigger
quote: This pullback can be treated as a standard pullback, with any of the standard pullback trigger entries.
description: After a confirmed breakout (G06-52), enter the resulting pullback with either standard pullback trigger (trend-line failure reversal G06-03, or support/resistance bounce G06-04).
pseudocode: G06-52 fired earlier AND (G06-03 OR G06-04) on the pullback following it
book_order_type: mixed: G06-03 is stop/market on the close-back bar, G06-04 is a limit entry

complexity.reason: the same pullback triggers applied after a confirmed breakout

name: AvoidHoldingPullbackBelowPrebreakoutPivotLow
quote: It is very hard to justify holding a simple breakout pullback that drops below the pivot low of the prebreakout base, as this type of action is much more indicative of a failed breakout.
description: Exit the breakout-pullback trade if price trades below (above) the low (high) of the prebreakout base -- a distinguishing invalidation level beyond the standard pullback stop.
pseudocode: low[0] < prebreakoutBaseLow
book_order_type: n/a (management exit, ahead of or in addition to the standard pullback stop)

complexity.reason: needs the prebreakout base's own low carried as position state from before entry

name: BreakoutFirstPullbackTemplate
quote: In some sense, this is a hybrid trade, combining characteristics of both breakout and pullback trades, but it can be simplified further: it is really nothing more than a simple pullback trade.
description: The book's named Breakouts, Entering on First Pullback Following template: setup (confirmed breakout, G06-52) + trigger (standard pullback trigger applied post-breakout, G06-53) + stop (standard pullback stop, plus the prebreakout-pivot invalidation G06-54) + standard pullback targets (G06-18, G06-19, G06-02).
pseudocode: G06-52 AND G06-53, managed by G06-17 (same as the plain Pullback template) and G06-54, targeting G06-18/G06-19/G06-02

complexity.reason: a thin wrapper around the plain pullback template with one extra invalidation level

notes: Trade type: support/resistance breaking. Trends from good breakout levels tend to run longer, so the book suggests holding more of the position for extension rather than taking full profits at the first target.

name: PullbackFarFromMaFilter
quote: A simple but effective trading rule could be instituted that simply prevents you from buying or selling pullbacks that are far away from a moving average, assuming that far away has been precisely defined.
description: Block a pullback-continuation long entry when the close is more than maxAtrMult times ATR above the reference moving average (i.e., price is overextended above the average rather than pulled back near it); mirrored below the average for shorts.
pseudocode: close[0] - ema(close, maLength) <= maxAtrMult * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: needs a moving average and an ATR, compared as a difference so it passes the shift test

notes: Grimes explicitly defers the 'far away' threshold to the trader ('assuming that far away has been precisely defined'); maxAtrMult=2.0 is a chosen default, expressed in ATR units per the shift-test convention rather than as a fixed price distance.
Very likely the same primitive as the catalog's CloseWithinAtrOfEma; recorded here as its own candidate per the dedup-hint convention.

name: HigherTimeframePullbackQualityFilter
quote: first review some of the characteristics that define high-probability pullbacks on a single time frame: Presence of a good impulse setting up further continuation. Market is not overextended. Market is not on the third (or later) trend leg. Absence of momentum divergence. Absence of buying or selling climax. Pullbacks show generally lower activity and volume than the trend legs.
description: Composite gate: on the higher-time-frame-approximated series, require an impulse leg present, no overextension beyond the HTF band, not the third-or-later trend leg, no momentum divergence and no climax bar, before trusting a lower-timeframe with-trend entry. 'Lower activity/volume than the trend legs' cannot be evaluated (see rejected volume items).
pseudocode: hasImpulseLeg(htfMultiplier) && !htfOverextended(kEmaLength, kAtrLength, kBandMult, htfMultiplier) && legCount(htfMultiplier) < 3 && !htfMomentumDivergence(htfMultiplier) && !htfClimaxBar(htfMultiplier)

complexity.reason: bundles leg counting, climax detection and divergence checks on an approximated higher time frame; each sub-criterion needs its own design decision (leg/pivot detection, climax definition) before this composite is codeable as a single gate

notes: Volume-based sub-criterion explicitly dropped: the engine has bar volume but the book's comparison is impressionistic ('generally lower activity'), not a stated threshold; left out rather than guessed.

Each named sub-condition (impulse leg, third-leg count, climax, divergence) likely already exists in some form in the Brooks corpus on the trading timeframe; this candidate is specifically about evaluating them on the htfMultiplier-approximated higher time frame.

name: ReenterToFullSizeAfterPullbackToEntryPostPartial
quote: consider a trader who gets into a trade, takes half of it off at a 1X profit ... and then finds the trade back at the entry price. This trader can add the half she already exited back to the trade
description: After partial profits were taken at 1x risk, if price pulls back to the original entry price while the remaining position is still open, add back the exited portion at the entry price.
pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() != 0 and partialProfitTaken == true and close[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() and close[0] >= ctx.EntryPrice() - reentryTolerance
book_order_type: limit re-entry at the entry price

complexity.reason: requires tracking whether a partial exit already occurred on this position, a state the single-net-position engine model may not expose cleanly

notes: Depends on partial-exit bookkeeping (a partialProfitTaken flag) that is not a standard ctx accessor; the authoring pass needs to decide whether the generator's position model can represent this at all.

name: Anti
quote: Anti A trade setup that attempts to enter the first pullback following a potential change of trend.
description: Enter on the first pullback that forms after price shows a potential change of trend direction.
pseudocode: trendChangeProxy(0) // e.g. close crosses the EMA against the prior trend and isFirstPullbackSinceSignal(0, maxBars)
book_order_type: n/a (setup identification; actual entry is the pullback-holds test, mechanized close-then-next-open)

complexity.reason: "potential change of trend" is not defined precisely by the glossary entry; a design decision (which trend-change proxy) is needed before coding

notes: The glossary gives only the name and one-line description; the operational trend-change test and pullback depth/duration are undefined and must be chosen by the authoring pass.
Depends on the pullback primitive (G16-16).

name: ComplexPullbackTwoLegAbcd
quote: A two-legged pullback that is a complete ABCD trend structure. These are common, especially in mature trends.
description: Classifies the current pullback as complex if it contains two internal counter-legs (an A-B-C-D structure) rather than one simple leg.
pseudocode: legCount(currentPullback, swingStrength) == 2

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to count internal legs within a bounded pullback window

notes: Feeds G16-25's rule-of-alternation classifier (simple vs. complex).

name: HighAndTightFlagShallowPullback
quote: A specific type of flag that holds near the high of a sharp up move (or near the low of a sharp decline) that often suggests strong buying (or selling) pressure behind the move. These often lead to sharp continuation.
description: After a sharp impulse leg, the pullback stays very shallow, holding near the impulse's extreme rather than giving back much of the move.
pseudocode: impulseRange = highest(high, impulseLookback) - lowest(low, impulseLookback); pullbackDepth(0) <= shallowFraction * impulseRange
book_order_type: n/a (context test); actual entry mechanized as close-then-next-open on a pullback-holds signal

complexity.reason: needs an impulse-leg measurement plus a pullback-depth-since-extreme test

notes: No numeric shallowFraction is given by Grimes; 0.25 chosen as a reasonable 'high and tight' default.

name: ImpulseMoveLargeDirectionalBar
quote: In technical analysis, a strong movement in the market, usually sharp and in one direction. Also called a momentum move.
description: Flags a short net directional move that is large relative to recent volatility, over a small number of bars.
pseudocode: abs(close[0] - close[legBars]) > impulseAtrMult * atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: a fixed-offset net-move comparison against an ATR

notes: "Momentum move" is glossed as a synonym on the same page (page 450); no separate candidate needed.

name: PullbackPrimitiveDefinition
quote: A general term for a consolidation pattern in a trend. Many of the traditional distinctions of technical analysis (flag, pennant, box, etc.) are not meaningful, as all pullback patterns can be traded according to similar rules.
description: A pullback is a counter-trend move (one or more bars against the prevailing trend direction) that has not yet produced a new trend extreme in the counter-trend direction.
pseudocode: close[0] < close[1] while priorTrendDirection == up and no new trend-direction extreme has been made since the pullback began

complexity.reason: Grimes deliberately declines to give a precise numeric boundary, saying sub-distinctions (flag, pennant, box) are not meaningful; a design decision is needed to operationalize where a pullback starts and ends

notes: Foundational primitive that G16-01 (Anti), G16-03 (complex pullback), and G16-08 (high and tight flag) depend on.
"Flag" (page 447) and "retracement" (page 453) are glossed as synonyms of pullback; no separate candidates needed.

name: TrendLegStructureImpulseRetracementImpulse
quote: In trend analysis, the third leg of the impulse-retracement-impulse unit that comprises the basic trend structure. Gauging the strength of the extension leg is one of the main ways to judge strength of the trend.
description: Defines the basic trend unit as three alternating swing legs (impulse, retracement, impulse-extension) and compares the third leg's length to the first (the 'preceding' or 'setup' leg) to judge trend strength.
pseudocode: leg3Length = abs(swingPivot(0) - swingPivot(1)); leg1Length = abs(swingPivot(2) - swingPivot(3)); leg3Length > extensionRatio * leg1Length

complexity.reason: needs three ranked, alternating swing legs and a ratio comparison between the first and third

notes: Collapses four related glossary terms into one candidate: 'extension' (p.446, the third leg), 'next trend leg' (p.451, the leg following a consolidation), 'preceding trend leg' / 'setup leg' (p.452/p.455, the leg that sets up the retracement).

name: RuleOfAlternationPullbackTypeSequence
quote: In Elliott wave theory, the idea that retracements in trends tend to alternate between simple and complex consolidations.
description: The current pullback's type (simple vs. complex, per G16-03's leg count) differs from the type of the pullback immediately before it.
pseudocode: pullbackType(current) != pullbackType(previous)  // types are 'simple' (1 leg) or 'complex' (2+ legs)

complexity.reason: requires the complex-pullback leg classifier (G16-03) plus a persistent memory of the previous pullback's classification, and Elliott theory is presented as a general tendency, not a hard rule

notes: Elliott wave theory is mentioned only in passing as this glossary entry's source; Grimes does not otherwise endorse or use it elsewhere in the book, so treat this as a low-priority, speculative candidate.
